questions.q: Regarded as a science, medicine encompasses medical science learning as well as personal, humanistic and professional attributes.

Mitosis is a method of direct division of a cell, consisting of a complex of various processes, by means of which one of the two daughter nuclei normally receives identical complements of the number of chromosomes characteristic of the somatic cells of the species.

Placenta is a maternal organ characteristic of true mammals during pregnancy, providing endocrine secretion and selective exchange of soluble, blood-borne substances through an apposition of uterine and trophoblastic vascularized parts.

Cyanosis is a bluish discoloration, applied especially to such discoloration of skin and mucous membranes due to excessive concentration of reduced hemoglobin in the blood. Cyanosis is usually present in left heart failure if not caused by a complication or by pulmonary edema.
Hepatomegaly is enlargement of the liver and is typically observed in right heart failure, but splenomegaly is uncommon except in prolonged passive congestion of the liver.

Ascites is an effusion and accumulation of serous fluid in the abdominal cavity. It begins as an initial sign of right heart failure, usually associated with systemic venous hypertension, peripheral edema, and hydrothorax.
Hemoptysis is expectoration of blood or of blood-strained sputum, which is observed with particular frequency in patients with advanced bicuspid stenosis.

The patient with orthopnea always has difficult breathing except that he is in an uptight position. Two-pillow orthopnea can be defined as orthopnea that is relieved by elevating the head and chest from the recumbent position by the use of two pillows.

Shock may be a condition of profound hemodynamic disturbance characterized by failure of the circulatory system to maintain adequate perfusion of vital organs. The clinical manifestations of hypovolemic or cardiogenic shock include hypotension, hyperventilation, cold, clammy, cyanotic skin, a weak and rapid pulse, oliguria, and mental confusion, combativeness, or anxiety.

Secondary hypertension is hypertension due to or associated with a variety of primary diseases, such as essential hypertension, renal disorders, disorders of the central nervous system, endocrine diseases, and vascular diseases.

Atherosclerosis is an extremely common form of arteriosclerosis in which deposits of yellowish plaques containing cholesterol, lipoid material, and lipophages are formed within the intima and inner media of large and medium-sized arteries.
Since side-stream smoke has a higher concentration than mainstream smoke of carcinogens, it is certain that the passive smoker is exposed to a much greater risk of lung cancer than the smoker is.

The bronchogenic cancer development includes the following steps: appearance of cytologically abnormal epithelial cells, localization of carcinomatous changes, invasion of tumor cells and metastasis of the tumor.

The sentence “Cigarette smoking causes cancer in humans and experimental animals in a dose-dependent manner.” Means that smoking leads to the development of lung cancer in both man and animal and makes them both become dependent on smoking.

Four types of tumors account for 95 per cent of all lung malignancies: squamous cell, adenocarcinoma, large cell, and small cell lung cancer. Among them small cell lung cancer is the only ling cancer that reacts adversely to chemotherapy in clinic setting.
The lung can be affected by a variety of tumors, among which bronchogenic carcinoma, a leading fatal neoplasm in America, caused about 135, 000 death in the United States in 1985.
The clinical signs of osteomalacia are essentially the same as those of rickets.
The clinical features of rickets vary greatly according to the underlying disorder.
In most cases, an accumulation of excess osteoid is the first thing to consider when we diagnose the disease of osteomalacia.
It is now generally believed that mineralization disorders are caused by the effect of vitamin D on production of normal collagen matrix.
Rickets and osteomalacia are characterized by defective bone and cartilage mineralization in children and adults.
Sex hormones are important in bone tissue activity in that they promote the growth of new bone.
Vertebra and certain facial bones are called irregular bones because they have different number in all individuals.
Osteoporosis in some elderly individuals is due to the decreased ability in the rate of protein formation.
In healthy adult, a delicate homeostasis is maintained between the action of osteoclasts and osteoclasts.
Long bones are curve-shaped bones which can bear body weight and provide extensive areas for muscle attachment.
Inadequate blood supply in relation to the metabolic requirements of active muscle, or frank ischemia from vascular occlusion, might lead to myopathic disease.
The motor end plate refers to a point at which the spinal cord joins a cranial nerve.
The muscle fibers are attached directly to the skeleton so that their contraction maintains posture and effects movement.
The myofibrils consist of longitudinally oriented interdigitating filaments of contractile proteins.
Making up nearly half of the weight if a male adult, striated muscle is susceptible to various diseases because of its complex structure.
Exercise may stimulate blood flow to a muscle.
Hypertrophy refers to the increased size of a muscle.
Striated muscles are involuntary ones and skeletal muscles are also called voluntary ones.
Movement of our body is mainly produced by the contraction of tendons.
Voluntary muscles are so named because they can control our own will.

Medicine has not been practiced in a scientific way throughout most of the recorded history of medicine and physicians, if not totally flawed, were nor sure what caused the diseases and how they should be treated.

Advances made in molecular and structural biology as well as in immunology and genetics are so impressive that other aspects of human science such as psychology, anthropology and sociology can be easily overlooked.
Premedical, medical, residency and continuing medical education are all integral parts of medical education in the United Stated.

The importance of biomedicine can never be too emphasized, for it lays the foundation for understanding disease, making diagnoses, applying new therapies and appreciating the complexities and opportunities of new technologies.

Being a physician means the commitment to lifelong learning, which requires that one have a complete understanding of the scientific basis not only to acquire and appreciate new theories, but also to apply them to the treatment of patients.

Numerous major clinical achievements indicate that more than 60% of the discoveries arise from the category of clinical application with a notion that basic research provides theories and guidelines for clinical treatment.

The list of our medical breakthroughs includes the control of infectious diseases, the regulation of blood pressure, fundamental immunology, fundamental genetics, and metabolic regulation by hormones, which are considered milestones in the course of medical history.
“Golden age of microbiology” refers to the period when Pasteur, working in Paris, and Robert Koch, working in Berlin, began to probe into the intricacies of infectious diseases.

Behavioral causes such as alcohol, drugs, violence, suicide, smoking and excessive aggression account for more than half the cost to the national health care, according to the National Center for Health Statistics of the United States.
Involuntary muscles make up the walls of the heart, intestines and other hollow tubes.
The more strongly a muscle contracts, the firmer the muscle is.
The muscle fibers will become more and more in number as one grows old.
The fibers of a muscle will become smaller if the nerve supply to it is cut.
When a tourniquet is applied to control arterial bleeding, it should remain tightened at least 20 minutes.
Muscle fibers are joined end to end by connective tissue in all muscles.
Normal muscle fibers are grouped into 2 classes, one rich in oxidative enzymes and the other in glycolytic enzymes.
Without the spindle afferent nerve impulses, the central nervous system could not monitor changes in muscle length.
As a matter of fact, no disease affects all muscles in the body, and each neuromuscular disease only involves particular muscles.
Since muscle possesses a limited capacity to regenerate, the loss of muscle fibers in all myopathic diseases is permanent.
Sufficient quantities of calcium and phosphorus must be included in the diet for bone growth and replacement.
Bone maturation and remodeling go on perpetually during the life of the individuals.
Both sutural and sesamoid bones are variable in number from person to person.
Osteoblasts are the cells responsible for the resorption of bone tissues.
Calcium stored in bone tissue can be distributed to other parts of the body on demand.
Mineralization of cartilage and bone is a complex process and depends in various factors.
Inadequate mineralization in rickets occurs in the matrix of cartilage in the growing epiphyseal plate.
Reduced mineralization activity may be observed without hyperosteoidosis in osteoporosis.
Clinical signs of osteomalacia are difficult to describe, for the disease-specific abnormalities may not be obvious, whereas features of an underlying disorder may predominate.
The radiographic abnormalities in both rickets and osteomalacia reflect the histopathologic changes.
Americans spend about $ 10 billion annually on the treatment of lung cancers, but still the majority of the patients will die of this disorder within one year of its detection.

Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death of men in 28 developed countries of the world. As for women, the mortality of lung cancer surpassed that of breast cancer for the first time in 1986 in the Unite Stated.
Lung cancer attacks male as well as female but there is a difference in the peak year of incidence.

Three important aspects of the cellular events that take place during the transformation of normal bronchial epithelial cells to malignant cells are: (1) damage to cellular deoxyribonucleic; (2) alteration in cellular oncogene expression; and (3) gene-derived factors that stimulate cellular division.
A recent study indicated that there existed a time lag in a particular population between a rise in deaths from lung cancer and that in cigarette consumption.

Heart failure is inability of the heart to pump blood at an adequate rate to fill tissue metabolic requirements or the ability to do so only ar an elevated filling pressure, It can be defined clinically as a syndrome of ventricular dysfunction accompanied by reduced exercise capacity and other characteristic hemodynamic, renal, neural, and hormonal responses.
Rheumatic heart disease is directly caused by streptococci, or is the most important manifestation of and sequel to rheumatic fever, consisting chiefly of valvular deformities.
Left venrtricular failure is characterized by signs of systemic venous congestion and peripheral edema, while right ventricular failure is dominated by symptoms of pulmonary congestion and edema.
Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea is an episode of respiratory distress that awakens patients from sleep and is not related to posture (especially reclining at night).

Right ventricular failure usually develops simultaneously with appearance of left ventricular failure. And in the presence of biventricular failure, signs of left ventricular failure may dominate, bur the presence of dyspnea and rales should suggest additional left ventricular failure.

Dyspnea is a typical manifestation of heart failure, especially right-side heart failure, is usually accompanied by an increased rate of breathing. The dyspnea relates to the increase in blood volume and interstitial fluid content of the lungs and ventilation increases. The patient is then aware of more severe shortness of breath.

During acute left ventricular failure, pulmonary arterial and capillary pressure can increase abruptly to so high a level as to exceed plasma oncotic pressure, with consequent rapid accumulation of edema fluid in the interstitial spaces.

Pregnancy is the condition of having a developing embryo or fetus in the body, after union of an ovum and spermatozoon. In women duration of pregnancy from conception to delivery is approximately 280 days.

Gene is a segment of a DNA molecule that contains all the information required for synthesis of a product, including both coding and non-coding sequences. It is the biological unit of heredity, self-reproducing, and transmitted from parent to progeny.

Meiosis is a special method of cell division, occurring in maturation of the sex cells, by means of which each daughter nucleus receives the same number of chromosomes characteristic of the somatic cells of the species.

questions.a: After injected into a muscle, Botox blocks nerve signals that tell your muscles to contract, temporarily smoothing out facial wrinkles, which is caused by muscle movement. 译文：略。
